best_plan.name: p2
best_plan.rationale: Plan p2 is the best cost-quality trade-off. It filters Reviews.csv to the target movie using the exact idx field, then scores each review from reviewText only with a lightweight semantic map. Compared with p1, p2 reduced token usage and cost substantially while slightly improving quality; compared with p3, it achieved much higher quality with similar cost and better latency. Across two executions, p2 delivered the top observed quality (~0.773-0.774 spearman) at low cost (~$0.0265) and the best end-to-end latency among the competitive plans.

plan_codes.p1:
pipeline = PhysicalPipeline(plan_name, "Reviews.csv", load_data("Reviews.csv"))
pipeline.filter(lambda row: row["idx"] == "ant_man_and_the_wasp_quantumania")
pipeline.sem_map(
    [{
        "name": "score",
        "type": int,
        "description": "An integer from 1 to 5 indicating how much the reviewer liked the movie based on the review text alone: 1=strongly disliked, 2=disliked, 3=mixed/neutral, 4=liked, 5=strongly liked."
    }],
    model=pz.Model.GOOGLE_GEMINI_2_5_FLASH_LITE
)
pipeline.project(["reviewId", "score"])
pipeline
plan_codes.p2:
pipeline = PhysicalPipeline(plan_name, "Reviews.csv", load_data("Reviews.csv"))
pipeline.filter(lambda row: row["idx"] == "ant_man_and_the_wasp_quantumania")
pipeline.sem_map(
    [{
        "name": "score",
        "type": int,
        "description": "Read only the review text and assign an integer score from 1 to 5 for how much the reviewer liked the movie: 1=very negative/disliked a lot, 2=negative, 3=mixed or lukewarm, 4=positive, 5=very positive/enthusiastic."
    }],
    model=pz.Model.GOOGLE_GEMINI_2_5_FLASH_LITE,
    depends_on=["reviewText"]
)
pipeline.project(["reviewId", "score"])
pipeline
